workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential on one branch and one pull request: implement -> test -> review round 1 (COMMENT; head still carries .legion/) -> implementer pushes the .legion/ deletion -> review round 2 (APPROVE naming the clean head C by SHA) -> retro (revived implementer, one docs/solutions/ commit + one Dispatch issue comment, no handoff) -> merger publishes READY to notifications.role.pr-queue -> the merge queue merges -> implementer confirms the marker on main and records it on the PR and the Dispatch issue -> architect signs off naming the merge commit (acceptance 4). The repository has no build, test suite, formatter, linter, or AGENTS.md: every check is a command against GitHub through `legion gh` whose output is recorded. No rebase unless GitHub reports mergeable CONFLICTING.

implement: legion-worker — supplies the whole implementer surface: path-scoped `jj split`, the bookmark -r @- push, the READY-format PR body with the `Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-153` line, re-run-not-repush for a red check, rebase only on CONFLICTING, the .legion/ deletion push at the reviewer's direction, and the post-merge production check; the same implementer is revived for retro under legion-retro and records on the Dispatch issue with the dispatch skill (`legion gh` refuses GitHub-issue writes).
test: legion-worker — defines the E2E section the tester writes into the PR body (real surface, exact command, observation, head SHA, one negative control) and the handoff commit/push gate; the surface here is the GitHub pull request itself (files, check-runs, contents API) and the negative control is the shim's refusal of `pr merge` (spec Testing).
review: legion-worker — one review per round via `legion gh -- api --method POST repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/<n>/reviews` with commit_id; COMMENT while .legion/ is on the head, APPROVE only the clean head named by SHA; CI, Threads, and E2E verified on GitHub never from a handoff; Thermo line omitted because the PR is a one-line markdown file (docs-only).

concerns: SPEC INCONSISTENCY (raised to the architect): Acceptance 1 says the pull request adds exactly one file 'at the reviewed and merged head', but Design says retro commits its learnings under docs/solutions/ on top of the approved head, so the MERGED head carries two files. This plan follows Design and both skills (legion-worker, legion-retro): acceptance 1 is proven at the approved head C (exactly one file), and the merged head is C plus exactly one docs/solutions/ file. Recommendation to the architect: amend acceptance 1 to name the approved head. If the architect rules that retro records learnings only as the Dispatch comment, retro commits nothing and the merger's `diff --summary` above C is quoted as `no file changes above the approved head`.

MERGE QUEUE NOT LIVE (raised to the architect): `envoy_role_get pr-queue` returned `no holder for role pr-queue` at 2026-09-13T15:03Z. The merger's `envoy_publish` to notifications.role.pr-queue is rejected 404 while no organizer holds the role, and no worker can merge (`legion gh` refuses `pr merge`; PR #38 and #33 were merged by app/legion-implementer under the merge queue's own credential). Acceptance 3 waits on a live queue; the merger reports a rejected publish to the architect instead of retrying in a loop.

.omp/config.yml LEAK RISK: the daemon writes an empty, unignored .omp/config.yml into the working copy on every worker spawn and jj snapshots it into @ (`jj status` shows `A .omp/config.yml`; the repository has no .gitignore). Every commit MUST be a path-scoped `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" split -m '<msg>' <paths>` so the file stays in the undescribed remainder @. Never `jj describe`/`jj commit` the whole working copy.

BOOKMARK PLACEMENT: after `jj split` the bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-153 stays on the remainder @ (verified on this jj 0.45.1 build in a scratch repo: `jj bookmark set <name> -r @-` is refused with 'Refusing to move bookmark backwards or sideways' and succeeds with --allow-backwards; pushing @ itself is refused because it has no description). Every push is `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-153 -r @- --allow-backwards && jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-153`. The only commit skipped is the undescribed working copy, which must never be pushed.

FOUR CHECK-RUNS PER HEAD: both workflows trigger on `push` and `pull_request`, so each head shows `check` twice (ci) and `gate` twice (fail-on-demand) — verified on PR #43 head 69d8dd37 and PR #44 head d9226786. `ci` sleeps 20 s: wait with `legion gh -- pr checks <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --watch` before reading conclusions. A red run is re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never by pushing.

BYTE COMPARISON: `cmp - <(printf …)` fails on this machine (cmp cannot seek a process substitution, exit 2 'Illegal seek', per the LEGSMOKE-134 plan). Write the expected literal to a file under /tmp and `cmp` against that file. Scratch files (PR body, review JSON, expected bytes) live under /tmp, never in the workspace — anything written under $LEGION_WORKSPACE is snapshotted into @.

TIMESTAMP IS CHOSEN BY THE IMPLEMENTER: the file name and its single line carry the UTC creation time, so no byte hash can be pre-computed here. The implementer records path, line, bytes, and sha256 in implement.json; the tester derives the expected bytes from the file NAME (the timestamp in the name and the line must be identical) and never from the handoff.

DOCS-ONLY PR: a single one-line markdown file, so per legion-worker the reviewer runs no thermonuclear pass and omits the Thermo line entirely. The architect may override; then the reviewer runs both thermo agents once at the round-1 head and adds the line.

GITHUB-ISSUE WRITES REFUSED: `legion gh` refuses every GitHub-issue write (including `gh issue comment`), so legion-retro's `gh issue comment` example and the post-merge 'record it on the issue' are dispatch_comment calls on LEGSMOKE-153 in plain English.

AFTER THE .legion/ DELETION PUSH nothing writes a handoff: cleanup, the APPROVE review, retro, the merger's READY, and the post-merge confirmation all report with `legion handoff complete` alone. Recreating .legion/ changes the approved head and restarts the review loop.

TRANSIENT RIG OUTAGES observed while planning (2026-09-13 ~14:40–14:50Z): dispatch_* tools returned 'Unable to connect' and envoy_* tools 'nats: connection closed' for a few minutes while envoy-dispatch and NATS restarted; both recovered without action. A worker seeing these errors retries once after ~30 s before reporting to the architect.

SIBLING BRANCHES: PRs #41 (legion/LEGSMOKE-132), #42 (legion/LEGSMOKE-131), #43 (legion/LEGSMOKE-137) are open and add different smoke/ files; a newer main after one of them merges is NOT a rebase trigger — only `mergeable: CONFLICTING` reported by GitHub is. main was 373184959b7a62c7e283f131564b8aeaad9365a2 when planned; the file is absent there and no PR or remote branch legion/LEGSMOKE-153 existed (verified 2026-09-13T14:5xZ).

fingerprintCommand: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" diff --from "fork_point(main@origin | <sha>)" --to <sha> --git --context 0 '~(.legion | docs/solutions)' | sed -e '/^@@/d' -e '/^index /d' | sha256sum
rebasePolicy: Rebase ONLY when `legion gh -- pr view $N --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --json mergeable --jq .mergeable` prints CONFLICTING (or the controller asks because of a conflict). A newer main, a red run, or a stale CI is never a reason. Sami, 2026-09-11: 'Please don't do unnecessary rebases (i.e. unless there are merge conflicts). The CI queue is too long and slow.'

Implementer only: BEFORE=$(fingerprint at current tip); `cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" rebase -s 'roots(main@origin..@)' -d main@origin` (whole chain); resolve; cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-153 -r @- --allow-backwards && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git push --bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-153 ; AFTER=$(fingerprint at new tip); `legion gh -- pr comment $N --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --body $'rebase <old-tip> → <new-tip>; fingerprint <BEFORE> → <AFTER>; unchanged|changed\n\n<!-- legion: {"session":"<session-id>","phase":"<phase>"} -->'`.

unchanged -> confirmation only: the tester re-checks the bare gates (four check-runs success at the new head) and edits the E2E head with `rebase re-check <old> → <new>: fingerprint unchanged, bare gates only`; a prior APPROVE gets one confirming APPROVE naming both SHAs. changed -> a full test round and one new review.
ciFailurePolicy: A failed check-run at any head: `legion gh -- run view <run-id> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --log-failed`. Flaky or infrastructure failure -> `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never a new commit. `ci` cannot fail on content (it only sleeps 20 s); `fail-on-demand` fails only if .fail-me exists at the repository root, which allowedPaths forbids — if it is red, someone pushed .fail-me and that is fixed in this PR. The PR is never published to the queue while any check-run is not success.

errors_fromSpec.checkRed: implementer reads the failed run; flaky -> rerun; real -> fix in this PR; never publish while red
errors_fromSpec.conflicting: implementer rebases once and posts before/after fingerprints; tester re-runs bare gates only if unchanged
errors_fromSpec.changesRequested: implementer resolves every thread (`legion threads resolve` before the push), then tester, then reviewer, in that order
errors_fromSpec.threadCannotBeResolved: architect opens an action ask naming the thread URL; merger does not publish while it is open
errors_fromSpec.closedUnmerged: architect reassesses: fresh implementer or cancel with a stated reason
